context: programme-scale · trunk infrastructure then districts · phased over years

brief.intro: A new city or master development is a phased programme, not a single project. New to this type? Picture it in layers over years: first mass earthworks and trunk infrastructure (roads, power, water, drainage, telecom), then districts of buildings, landmarks and public realm built out parcel by parcel. The critical path is the enablement and phasing of serviced land — bringing utilities to each parcel's boundary in the right order — not any one building. Success is about sequencing infrastructure ahead of the districts it serves and managing the interfaces between many concurrent packages.

scope.name: Master enabling & mass earthworks
scope.desc: Land preparation, bulk cut/fill, haul roads and site-wide grading.

scope.name: Trunk roads & corridors
scope.desc: Primary road network and the service corridors that carry the utilities.

scope.name: Trunk power & substations
scope.desc: Bulk-supply substations and the HV/MV distribution network.

scope.name: Trunk water & wastewater
scope.desc: Potable water, wastewater and pump/lift stations feeding the districts.

scope.name: Stormwater & drainage
scope.desc: Site-wide stormwater network, attenuation and outfalls.

scope.name: Telecom & smart-city ducting
scope.desc: City-wide communications ducting, ITS and smart-city backbone.

scope.name: District / parcel civils
scope.desc: Local roads, utilities and grading that make each parcel a serviced plot.

scope.name: Buildings & landmarks
scope.desc: Residential, commercial and landmark buildings by parcel (their own programmes).

scope.name: Public realm & landscape
scope.desc: Parks, plazas, streetscape and landscape between the buildings.

scope.name: District handover & integration
scope.desc: Energising and testing networks and handing serviced parcels / districts over in phases.

must_get_right: Sequence trunk infrastructure ahead of the districts it serves — serviced-land handover drives everything downstream.
Phase the programme so land is released in the order the market and construction need it.
Trunk power and water energisation gate district construction — protect those milestones.
Manage the interfaces between many concurrent packages; shared haul roads, corridors and utilities are the clash points.
It is a rolling programme with staged handovers — plan it as phases and milestones, not one finish date.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A programme-level Critical Path Method (CPM) network in Primavera P6, interface- and milestone-driven, developed to a Level 2–3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Sub-programmes (infrastructure, each district) integrate at serviced-land handover and utility-energisation milestones; total float kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Bulk earthworks and infrastructure on a 6-day week with seasonal / weather allowances; district building programmes run on their own calendars. Long-duration phases are planned in years with rolling lookaheads.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path is infrastructure-led: enabling & mass earthworks → trunk roads & corridors → trunk power/water/drainage energisation → serviced-parcel handover → district buildings → public realm → phase handover. Serviced-land availability, not any single building, governs the programme.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Master-plan phasing and funding are committed per phase; authority approvals and off-site connections are secured to the phasing dates; developer/parcel uptake follows the release plan; and interface agreements between packages are in place.

sections.heading: Procurement, phasing & long-lead items
sections.body: The programme is phasing- and interface-driven; the main drivers are serviced-land milestones and a few trunk long-leads, tracked as milestones:

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Many concurrent packages sharing haul roads, corridors and temporary utilities; dust, traffic and environmental controls across a large live site; and coordination of numerous contractors are the dominant constraints.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: phasing / funding slippage, trunk utility energisation delay, and interface clashes between concurrent packages. Contingency is held at each phase gate and before each serviced-land handover.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (programme milestones) and Level 2 (phase summary) to stakeholders, controlled at Level 3, with each district expanded to Level 4–5 — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
